key_insight: Quantum-Audit introduces a large, focused benchmark (2,700 questions) that systematically measures how well language models understand core quantum computing concepts, revealing concrete reasoning limits beyond code/circuit generation.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks focus on quantum code and circuit design but do not measure conceptual understanding and reasoning in quantum computing; this paper fills that evaluation gap.
method: Curate a 2,700-question benchmark covering core quantum topics (theory, algorithms, gates/measurement, noise and complexity).
Evaluate a wide set of language models on the benchmark using accuracy and qualitative reasoning/error analyses.
Analyze failure modes to map where models misunderstand concepts versus where they can reliably assist users.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a diagnostic tool to assess and improve LLM reliability on quantum computing tasks, guiding model selection, fine-tuning, and dataset creation for scientific QA and education.
visual_elements: Topic-wise performance heatmap showing strengths/weaknesses across quantum subtopics
Leaderboard bar chart of model accuracies with confidence/error bars
Difficulty distribution histogram and example Q&A pairs illustrating typical failure modes
Flow diagram of the benchmark creation and evaluation pipeline (question sourcing → labeling → model testing → analysis)
paper_title: Quantum-Audit: Evaluating the Reasoning Limits of LLMs on Quantum Computing
paper_authors: Mohamed Afane, Kayla Laufer, Wenqi Wei, Ying Mao, Junaid Farooq
